title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). We document two preregistration/analysis issues evident in the archived artifacts: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per-condition generation, and (2) a prespecified comparison (GVR vs a schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, the results show that bounded GVR provides no additional verifier-detectable benefit when the generator+prompting combination already yields verifier-acceptable candidates in this synthetic workload; they do not generalize beyond the executed semantics, model, task bank, or verifier. We release and analyze the authoritative archived artifacts and recommend reproducible follow-ups (independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model runs, and expanded verifier coverage).

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiency but raises safety and correctness concerns: stochastic generators can emit syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, required workflows, or security predicates). Prior work therefore recommends architectures that interpose deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects prior to execution.

We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment to test a focused operational question: under a frozen, archived design that used a single generator/prompt pairing and shared-initial-candidate generation semantics, does inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to an unconstrained baseline? The preregistration and full execution artifacts are archived and authoritative for all reported numbers (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d).

Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation on a public synthetic NetOps task bank (240 paired tasks) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic pybatfish-style verifier; (2) transparent execution accounting showing that shared-initial-candidate semantics produced one generation per task reused across arms (model_calls_used = 240) and that every generation satisfied the verifier (n11 = 240); (3) confirmatory statistics reporting a degenerate null (paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0], bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729) together with an explicit reconciliation of preregistered power assumptions and executed semantics; and (4) operationally grounded recommendations and reproducible next steps to evaluate GVR under conditions that restore discordance potential and adversarial sensitivity.
sections.related_work:
The study connects to three literatures relevant to LLMs and NetOps reliability. First, surveys and empirical studies across domains document hallucinations and fabricated outputs by LLMs for code and structured artifacts, motivating deterministic validators in downstream pipelines (see evidence synthesis entries and the supplied bibliography). Second, generate–verify–repair and constrained-decoding techniques have been shown to improve mechanically checkable properties (compilation, grammar validity) in prior work; reported case studies suggest these architectures reduce surface-level failures but leave open questions about semantic correctness on domain-specific invariants. Third, NetOps-specific literature emphasizes verifier-driven evaluation (reachability and policy invariants), intent-based translation systems, and human-in-the-loop governance for high-stakes changes.

This run differs from many prior studies because it was fully preregistered, used a paired confirmatory design, and required an authoritative archived analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). Unlike broader benchmark comparisons that report aggregate model performance, our experiment evaluated whether a bounded GVR intervention reduces verifier-detected semantic failures in a tightly specified synthetic workload with explicit validator predicates. The supplied evidence map (manuscript_evidence_bundle and evidence_synthesis) informed our experimental choices and situates the present null outcome within the broader set of findings that (a) constrained decoding and verification improve syntactic/executable rates but (b) verifier coverage and evaluation semantics crucially condition measurable benefit.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands: The study was preregistered as study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1. The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion difference in verifier-detected semantic-violation rate, computed in paired fashion). Two prespecified primary comparisons were listed in the preregistration: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding, with Bonferroni correction across the two comparisons (family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). The preregistered analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' was frozen prior to execution.

Design and frozen execution contract: Confirmatory sample: N = 240 tasks constituted as 12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks per cluster. The adapter configuration that executed the run is archived (adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Requested model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Crucial frozen semantics recorded in the preregistration and manifest: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded single repair attempt); maximum_model_calls budget = 480; execution_mode = scientific_confirmatory. The preregistration and execution manifest were archived prior to generation (preregistration_sha256 given above).

Rationale and power plan: The preregistered power and precision plan targeted a detectable absolute paired reduction of 10 percentage points with N = 240 under assumptions of independent per-condition generation and plausible discordance. Power calculations were frozen in the preregistration and are authoritative for the intended independent-generation design. The execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (documented in the manifest), which deterministically affects discordance potential and therefore invalidates the preregistered power assumption for the executed run.

Task bank, oracle, and scoring: The public synthetic NetOps task bank encodes initial device states, intent descriptions, workflow constraints, and expected final states; the archived task manifest and representative scoring artifacts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json) provide per-task difficulty metadata. The deterministic validator implements pybatfish-style checks returning structured diagnostics (violation_count, violations list, parsed_command_count, required_command_count). Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation as implemented by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0). Representative per-task validation_before and validation_after traces are archived and used for all scoring decisions.

Execution controls, missingness, and contamination: The preregistration defined exclusion rules and a missingness plan ('complete_pair_primary'); pairs with irrecoverable infrastructure/model-call failures would be handled per executor rules. The execution manifest (execution_manifest) records planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 240; contamination and missingness summaries are archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv and analysis/missingness_summary.csv) and report zero flags and zero failures.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting (artifact-backed): The archived execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 240, and model_calls_used = 240 under the shared-initial-candidate semantics. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) confirm episode accounting consistency and provider-call audit details. Representative scored artifacts under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ show that for every task the shared initial candidate (shared-initial generation) was identical to both arm responses.

Primary confirmatory outcomes: The registered analysis executor produced the following contingency table: n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Summary rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (method = paired_bootstrap_percentile; bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and analysis/results.json are archived and authoritative for these numbers.

Repair usage and trigger diagnostics: For every episode the validator trace shows repair_applied = false. The bounded repair loop never executed because the shared initial candidate already satisfied validator predicates for every task. Representative per-task scoring JSON (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and task-000001-guarded.json) record validator validation_before and validation_after blocks with violation_count = 0 and validator_id deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The contamination_summary.csv is empty and missingness_summary.csv records zero failures.

Statistical interpretation and degeneracy: The observed contingency (zero discordant pairs) makes the paired McNemar test degenerate: no within-pair disagreements exist to estimate a differential effect. The exact-test p = 1.00 and the bootstrap CI collapsing to [0.0, 0.0] are deterministic consequences of the observed contingency and the preregistered analysis procedures. Because the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation (restoring discordance potential), that power calculation does not apply to the executed shared-generation design; the manifest documents this mismatch and its deterministic consequences.

Unexecuted prespecified comparison: The preregistration specified two primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B). The archived execution artifacts document only the adapter-configured paired experiment comparing the unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared_initial_candidate semantics; the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale for its omission appears in the execution artifacts. We explicitly disclose this prespecified-but-unexecuted comparison as a procedural deviation and an unresolved limitation of the present run.
sections.discussion:
Conservative interpretation: The artifact-backed null result demonstrates that, under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics and for the supplied synthetic workload and verifier predicates, a bounded GVR intervention (one allowed repair) produced no verifier-detectable benefit because the generator+prompting pairing already produced verifier-acceptable outputs for every task. Two non-exclusive artifact-supported mechanisms explain the outcome. First, task/verifier alignment: the synthetic task bank, the prompt and generator pairing, and the deterministic validator together defined a distribution the generator could satisfy deterministically. Second, sensitivity reduction from shared-generation semantics: reusing a single shared initial candidate across arms removes independent stochastic variation and therefore removes the within-pair discordance that GVR could exploit.

Implications for evaluation practice: Measuring the operational value of GVR requires evaluation semantics aligned with the inferential assumptions. If the objective is to establish that GVR reduces verifier-detected violations under generator stochasticity, the evaluation must permit independent per-condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true), include adversarial or golden-reference tasks that reliably induce verifier failures, or test across multiple generator families and prompt variants. The archived artifacts already contain the task manifest, RNG seeds, and adapter configuration; toggling generation_semantics and rerunning using the same archived inputs would restore the preregistered design logic and make the preregistered power arguments applicable.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is impacted by the preregistration/power mismatch: the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation, which the executed shared-generation semantics violated. Construct validity is limited by verifier completeness: passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 does not guarantee absence of all operational risks outside the validator's encoded invariants. External validity is constrained by the synthetic task bank, a single generator (gpt-5-mini), a single bounded repair budget (one attempt), and a single verifier implementation. Conclusion validity is limited because zero discordant outcomes preclude evidence for GVR efficacy under the executed semantics. These threats are enumerated and discussed in the archived limitations and deterministic reconciliation artifacts.

Operational recommendations grounded in the archive: (1) Re-execute the preregistered paired design with independent per-condition generation (set independent_condition_generation = true) to restore discordance potential; the same task manifest and RNG seeds are archived to support deterministic reruns. (2) Inject adversarial or golden tasks (the preregistration planned 10% golden tasks) whose expected verifier outcome is known, to validate verifier sensitivity and prevent oracle complacency. (3) Expand the generator scope beyond gpt-5-mini to measure cross-model generality. (4) Increase or allow iterative repair budgets and record repair iteration distributions; the current artifacts record repair_applied = false for all episodes. (5) Broaden verifier coverage (additional semantic invariants or formal/SMT hybrids) to reduce oracle incompleteness risk; the evidence_synthesis identifies G2 (integration with formal verification) as an open gap.

Relation to prior findings: Our results align with prior literature that emphasizes (a) the usefulness of verifier-interposed pipelines in reducing mechanically checkable errors but (b) the dependence of measurable benefit on evaluation semantics and verifier completeness. The null outcome in the executed shared-generation setting highlights that experimental design choices (shared vs independent generation, adversarial injection) materially alter the ability to empirically demonstrate GVR benefits.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics (one shared generation per task reused across arms), every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a null paired estimate (0.0), exact McNemar p = 1.00, and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR did not add verifier-detectable value in this specific, artifact-grounded setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. However, two preregistration/execution deviations materially constrain inference: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption; and (2) a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no rationale is recorded in the archive. We therefore do not generalize beyond the specific model, prompt, task bank, verifier, repair budget, or generation semantics. We publish and release the authoritative archived artifacts so others can reproduce the accounting and extend the evaluation under independent-generation, adversarial, and multi-model regimes to more robustly assess GVR’s operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
